<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|368|THE ACTES|CHA. XXVII.}}</noinclude>Centurion beleeued the gouernour and maister of the ship, more then those things vvhich vvere said of Paul. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=12}}† And vvhereas it vvas not a commodious hauen to vvinter in, very many taking counsel appointed to saile thence, if by any meanes they might comming to Phœníce, vvinter there, a hauen of Crete looking tovvard the {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ names of vvindes.}}∷ Afrike and the Chore. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=13}}† And the southvvinde blovving, they thinking that they had obteined their purpose, vvhen they had parted from Asson, sailed along by Crete. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=14}}† But not long after, a tempestuous vvinde that is called Euro-aquilo, droue against it. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=15}}† And vvhen the shippe vvas caught and could not make vvay against the vvinde, giuing vp the ship to the vvindes, vve vvere driuen. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=16}}† And running vpon a certaine iland, that is called {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Græc. Clauda.}}∷ Cauda, vve could scarse get the cock-boate. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=17}}† Vvhich being taken vp, they vsed helps, girding the ship, and fearing lest they should fall into {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ c a place of quicke sands.}}∷ the Syrte, letting dovvne the vessel, so vvere they caried. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=18}}† And vvhen vve vvere mightily tossed vvith the tempest, the next day they cast forth, {{verse|chapter=27|verse=19}}† And the third day vvith their ovvne handes they threvve forth the tacklinges of the ship. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=20}}† And neither sunne, nor starres appearing for many daies, and no smal storme being tovvard, al hope vvas novv taken avvay of our sauing.

{{verse|chapter=27|verse=21}}† And vvhen there had been long fasting, then Paul standing in the middes of them, said, You should in deede, O ye men, haue heard me, and not haue parted from Crete, & haue gained this hurt and losse. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=22}}† And novv I exhort you to be of good cheere. for there shal be no losse of any soule among you, but of the ship. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=23}}† For {{sup|‖}} an Angel of the God vvhose I am, and {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''ᾧ λατρεύω''.}}∷ vvhom I serue, stoode by me this night, {{verse|chapter=27|verse=24}}† saying, Feare not Paul, thou must appeare before Cæsar: and behold God hath {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Paul (saith S. Hierom) had so many soules in the ship giuen him, that is, so many men saued for his sake: and after he is vvith Christ, shal he shut his mouth, and not be able once to speake for them that haue beleeued in his Gospel? ''Hiero.adu. vigil''. Vvhereby he proueth that if God do much for the merits of Saincts in this life, much more at their intercession & praier in heauen.}}∷ giuen thee al that saile vvith thee. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=25}}† For the vvhich cause be of good cheere ye men: for I beleeue God, that it shal so be, as it hath been said to me. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=26}}† And vve must come vnto a certaine iland. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=27}}† But after the fourtenth night vvas come on vs, as vve vvere sailing in Adria about midnight, the shipmen deemed that there appeared some countrie to them. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=28}}† Vvho also sounding, found tvventie fadomes: and being parted a litle from thence, they found fiftene fadomes. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=29}}† And fearing lest vve should fall into rough places, casting out of the sterne foure ankers, they vvished<noinclude>{{rh|||that}}</noinclude>
